source.title: Adaptation Odyssey in LLMs: Why Does Additional Pretraining Sometimes Fail to Improve?
source.authors: Firat Öncel; Matthias Bethge; B. Ermi̇ş; M. Ravanelli; Cem Subakan; Çağatay Yıldız

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, though figures and some tables are flattened; exact plotted values cannot be recovered.
record.tranche_reason: Reports that additional pretraining can worsen same-domain test perplexity and that the effect depends on domain similarity and model capacity. These findings refine the broad expectation that training on natural data improves held-out performance, but do not test any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The paper studies additional pretraining of language models and reports test perplexity, not random-label memorization, classification error, or the specific interventions and measurements in V1–V8. Domain-by-domain values appear in figures and are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study measures within-domain perplexity after additional language-model pretraining. It neither tests nor uses any specific finding in V1–V8. Its domain-similarity and model-capacity results do not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, architecture comparisons, optimizers, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors report that additional pretraining can worsen within-domain test perplexity, associate degradation with greater similarity to the original pretraining corpus, and observe smaller adaptation effects in larger models. They also emphasize that a few special tokens account for much of the degradation, limiting perplexity as evidence of domain-specific improvement. These observations do not establish causation or downstream performance changes.
record.recipe_differences: Additional pretraining of decoder-only language models on natural text domains, evaluated by within-domain perplexity; the listed versions concern other training interventions, models, or generalization measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies between Wiki and S2ORC domains; degradation is reported to be smaller as model capacity increases. The paper reports that Wiki domains are more similar to original corpora.

fits_no_version.finding: After one epoch of additional pretraining, the authors report worse within-domain perplexity on Wiki domains and improved perplexity on S2ORC domains. Degradation is associated with greater similarity to the original corpus; larger models show smaller changes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Additional language-model pretraining can worsen within-domain perplexity, with outcomes associated with adaptation-domain similarity and model capacity.

fits_no_version.finding: On selected Wiki domains, reevaluated losses or perplexities on previously seen training data and held-out data increase during adaptation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: During one-pass language-model adaptation, performance on earlier training examples and same-domain held-out examples can deteriorate.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors attribute much of the perplexity degradation to a few frequent, domain-uninformative special tokens; Figure 4 illustrates OLMo-1B on the training portion of Human activities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aggregate perplexity changes after domain adaptation can be dominated by special tokens and may inadequately represent domain-specific improvement.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The study evaluates adaptation using perplexity alone and notes that downstream performance would also be useful. Figure 1 selects the 20 most extreme domains for each experiment; exact plotted values are not available in the supplied text. The training-curve examples are limited to four randomly chosen domains and one epoch.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy under the same training recipe.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error. Comparing pretrained model sizes does not test this intervention.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance and the effects of tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Identifying and removing memorized examples, retraining, and comparison with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T5 classification invokes a broader claim than V1–V8. No verdict applies to those versions. States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, although the text states the directions of the unrelated perplexity effects. The methods describe 20 selected adaptation domains, while Results describes selecting the 20 most extreme domains for display; the supplied text does not resolve that reporting ambiguity.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy, including chance performance on random labels.
Width sweeps past the interpolation threshold in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and optimizer tuning.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Additional pretraining on each selected M2D2 domain individually; test perplexity compared with zero-shot perplexity.
rows.measure: Test perplexity change (zero-shot versus adapted); text reports degradation on Wiki domains, exact values shown only in Figure 1.
rows.note: The paper reports a consistent Wiki-domain degradation across model sizes; numerical domain-level values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Wiki perplexity degradation is reported, but it is not a reversal of any listed version. Figure 1 displays selected extreme domains; exact values are unavailable.
